acceptance: A PR based on a commit whose baseline is still being built no longer reports a plain failure (it waits, falls back to a site-equivalent ancestor, or reports pending), or a decision to keep the failure is recorded with the reason
Any fallback uses only site-equivalent ancestors, with a test or recorded run showing a non-equivalent ancestor is not used
Any workflow change merged through the normal PR flow

description:
"Public-site visual regression" failed on #2831 (run 37961549887, job 113945316700) and on #2823 with "Error: No unexpired protected public-site visual baseline is bound to base SHA 08cf03c5eb8a... or a site-equivalent ancestor" (results-explorer/scripts/download-public-site-visual-baseline.mjs:50). Among the 10 most recently merged PRs on 2026-10-09, 2 failed this way, 6 passed and 2 skipped. The check is not required, so it does not block merges, but it teaches people to ignore a red check.

Root cause (verified): the baseline for base 08cf03c5e is built by the Documentation push run 37961232034, which ran 16:44-18:05 UTC. The failing visual job 113945316700 ran 17:40-17:44 UTC, before that baseline existed. The long Documentation run is itself partly queue delay (see actions-runner-queue-oracle-latency-20261009).

The site-equivalent-ancestor fallback (the `baseline_candidates` loop in .github/workflows/docs.yml, lines 89-94) rarely helps. It walks first-parent ancestors only while the diff to the base is empty over SITE_PATHS, and SITE_PATHS includes all of scripts/ (docs.yml:74-80), so almost any develop commit breaks equivalence. The wait knob PUBLIC_SITE_VISUAL_BASELINE_WAIT_SECONDS (download-public-site-visual-baseline.mjs:16, default 0) is not set in the job's env in ci.yml:1687-1696.

Options:
- set PUBLIC_SITE_VISUAL_BASELINE_WAIT_SECONDS in ci.yml so the job waits for the baseline;
- narrow SITE_PATHS (for example scripts/ to the files the site build actually reads) so the ancestor fallback finds a candidate;
- report "baseline pending" as a neutral or skipped result instead of a failure.

Guardrails. Do not weaken the visual comparison itself. A fallback to the "newest available ancestor" must stay site-equivalent (no diff over the site paths between that ancestor and the base); otherwise the comparison would be made against a different site. Related: astro-site-51-visual-gate-transition.
